How it works

THREE WAYS TO TEST YOUR FTP

FTP (Functional Threshold Power) is roughly the highest power you can hold for about an hour. Few people want to ride flat out for an hour, so shorter tests estimate it with a standard factor:

  • Ramp test: the power steps up every minute until you can't continue. FTP = 75% of your best 1-minute power. Quick and easy to pace, but it can over-estimate FTP for riders with a strong sprint.
  • 8-minute test: two 8-minute all-out efforts with 10 minutes' recovery between them. FTP = 90% of the better (or average) effort.
  • 20-minute test: one 20-minute all-out effort after a proper warm-up. FTP = 95% of your average power. The most widely used test.

Make the test count

Test when you're fresh, warm up well, and use the same test, bike and trainer each time so your numbers are comparable. Re-test every 6 to 8 weeks. For a fuller picture than one number, our Critical Power calculator uses two or three efforts.
